tester.task:
Write the tests that pin the attached spec's requirements.

- Put each test in the file the requirement's acceptance item names, adding to it where it exists. Add a case to an
  existing table or `test.each` over the same function before writing a new test. When an acceptance item names several
  files for one requirement, pin it once, in the lowest-level file that reaches it.
- Where the spec leaves an output's exact text open, pin what it does fix, such as that the input is refused and the
  path the refusal names, and never match the text loosely.
- Where the spec names conditions that combine, such as where a value is set and where it points, pin each combination
  as a row of one table.
- Leave your files formatted: run `check format`, and fix with `just fmt`.

Then give your `map` field, naming every requirement in exactly one list, its `requirement` opening with its id, as
`R1: …`:

- `pinned`: a requirement you pinned, with its test's repo-relative `file` and its `test` name exactly as the test call
  gives it, without any enclosing `describe`.
- `deferred`: a requirement only a name the build adds can reach, as that name is the builder's to design, or whose only
  check is text the spec leaves open, with why. The builder writes its test.
- `untestable`: a requirement no test can pin, such as a doc's wording, with why.

spec.hint: first, for the requirements to pin

writer.task:
Write the body of the pull request for the attached change to `pr.md`, for the owner who reviews it. Read the spec, then
the patches, then only as much of the lane as a section needs. When `revised` is attached, the patches revise that PR:
the body covers both as one change, the PR's whole diff. Write no title and no `Closes` line: the tour manager adds
them, with the gaps, the spend and the risk. Add no attribution, emoji or sign-off.

The spec picks the form:

- **Direct**, a spec opening with `#### Brief`: no spec gate ran, so the body shows the calls the builder made.
- **Specced**, a spec opening with `#### Context`: the owner approved its shape, so the body shows how the change holds
  to it.

Use exactly the form's sections, with no preamble, in the words of `GLOSSARY.md`. Size each section to the change: a
small change gets a sentence per section.

Direct:

```text
## Context

<a sentence or two: the problem and the intent>

## Shape

<one figure, footnoted with the calls the builder made>

## Evidence

- **Before:** <what failed or was missing>
  **After:** <the test or output that now passes>

## Merge Danger

<door and blast radius>
```

Specced:

```text
## Summary

<one line: built to spec, shape unchanged or not>

## Evidence

| Requirement | Pinned by |
| ----------- | --------- |
| R1          | <test>    |

## Off spec

<one line per drift, or "None.">

## Merge Danger

<door and blast radius>
```

## Shape

Draw the change by Figures below: the caption when it has one, the fenced source, then its notes as a numbered list. The
notes are the builder's own calls, read from the patches; with no spec gate, they are what the owner reviews. When no
figure fits, say the shape in a sentence.

## Evidence

Nothing ran for you here: the gate passed before you, so cite the tests the patches add or the spec's acceptance names,
never a run you did not see.

- **Direct:** Before is what the issue asked for, failing or missing. After names the test that now pins it, as
  pseudocode of its inputs and outcome, or the command output that shows it. Give one pair for the change the issue
  asked for, and at most two more for what the owner would otherwise check by hand, each Before and After one short
  line.
- **Specced:** one row per requirement, in order, naming the test that pins it: the acceptance item whose `# R` comment
  names it, or a test the patches add. A requirement no test pins says so in its row.
- **Map:** when the task has a `## map` section, a tester pinned the requirements, and its tests take the place of the
  acceptance items: each row or pair names the map's test, by file and name, or for a deferred requirement the test the
  patches add. An untestable requirement says so, with its why.

## Off spec

A drift is where the change departs from the approved spec: a requirement met otherwise than written, a decision taken
another way, a path outside Touches, a figure the patches no longer match. Give each one line. Redraw a spec figure, by
Figures below, only when the shape moved.

## Merge Danger

Use exactly:

```text
**Door:** <one-way or two-way>

<optional: one line on why>

**Blast Radius:** <one word>

<optional: what could break on merge>
```

A two-way door can be walked back by reverting. A one-way door cannot: a removed command, flag or file format, a changed
record, IR or config schema, data written that an older build cannot read. The blast radius names who feels a bad merge,
such as `cli`, `factory`, `compositions` or `docs`.


## Plain English

Write prose the reader takes in on one pass, most of the way to ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: keep its
writing rules, not its controlled dictionary.

- One idea per sentence: at most 20 words for an instruction, 25 for a description, 30 for a requirement.
- One topic per paragraph, in at most six sentences.
- Active voice and simple tenses: "the tick posts the spec", not "the spec is being posted".
- One term for one thing, the term `GLOSSARY.md` uses, and one meaning per term.
- Keep the articles and the small words; do not drop them to save space.
- No stack of more than three nouns: "the findings of the check", not "spec check finding list".
- Plain verbs, not phrasal verbs or verbs made into nouns: "decide", not "make a decision on".
- Code, paths, flags and identifiers stay as written, in backticks.


## Figures

A figure draws the change's shape. Its notes are the design calls it shows, each pointed at by a superscript (`¹`, `²`)
in a label. Draw first, then write: a call a figure shows is a note on it, not prose beside it. The owner reads the
rendered figure; agents read its source and notes as text, so a figure says in a few lines what a paragraph would.

Pick the kind by what the change does to the system. Most changes need one figure or none, and none needs more than two.

| Kind          | Source            | Draw when                                                                 |
| ------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `seams`       | `flowchart`       | modules gain, lose or move a dependency: before and after                 |
| `sequence`    | `sequenceDiagram` | a flow across seams is new or changes order                               |
| `state`       | `flowchart`       | a lifecycle gains or changes a state or a move                            |
| `interface`   | `classDiagram`    | a module's public interface grows or shrinks: its depth, before and after |
| `contract`    | `classDiagram`    | the change sets or changes a one-way door: its shape after                |
| `composition` | `flowchart`       | a concert gains, drops or rewires a seat                                  |
| `call-tree`   | `diff`            | no template fits, and the point is a call added, dropped or moved         |
| `file-tree`   | `diff`            | no template fits, and the point is files added, moved or split            |
| `pseudocode`  | `diff`            | no template fits, and the point is logic in one place                     |

When no sketch says it faster than a sentence, draw nothing. Never write Mermaid outside these skeletons.

### Figure rules

1. **Text stays complete.** Every fact a figure shows is in a label or a note, so the spec reads whole unrendered.
   Colour, bold and dotted lines never carry a fact alone; the caption says what each styling means, or is empty.
2. **Labels are tags.** A node is a name (`route.ts`), an edge one to three words (`[tick] PR`). Detail goes in a note.
3. **Notes.** Superscripts run `¹` on in source order; the notes give each its note, in order, one fact each, a
   reference as a plain last note "In <path>".
4. **One idea per figure,** a dozen nodes at most. Draw only the modules, calls and states the change touches.
5. **Parse-safe labels.** Quote any flowchart label with spaces or punctuation; a `classDiagram` relation label stays
   bare. No `;`, no second `:`, no `/` outside quotes, no `<n>`.
6. **No fills.** The forge sets fill and text colour per theme. Highlight with a stroke from the palette only.

| Role  | Meaning                    | Node                                             | Edge                                            |
| ----- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| owner | waits on, or is, the human | `classDef owner stroke:#d4a72c,stroke-width:3px` |                                                 |
| agent | an agent acts, or new      | `classDef agent stroke:#4c9be8,stroke-width:3px` |                                                 |
| fault | a fault, or removed        | `classDef fault stroke:#e5534b,stroke-width:3px` | `linkStyle <i> stroke:#e5534b,stroke-width:3px` |
| done  | a success, or added        | `classDef done stroke:#57ab5a,stroke-width:3px`  | `linkStyle <i> stroke:#57ab5a,stroke-width:3px` |

`linkStyle` counts the links from 0 in source order, `~~~` included. Shapes: `["x"]` a step or state, `(["x"])` a start,
end or outside system, `{"x?"}` a decision. Edges: `-->` the normal move, `==>` the owner's move, `-.->` an exception, a
side effect or a dependency that goes.

### Skeletons

`seams`; keep `before ~~~ after` after every edge, or Mermaid may stack "after" above "before":

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph before ["before"]
    direction TB
    a1["module"] -.->|"dependency ¹"| b1["module"]
    b1 --> c1["module"]
  end
  subgraph after ["after"]
    direction TB
    a2["module"] -->|"dependency ²"| c2["module"]
    b2["module"] --> c2
  end
  before ~~~ after
  linkStyle 0 stroke:#e5534b,stroke-width:3px
  linkStyle 2 stroke:#57ab5a,stroke-width:3px
```

`sequence`:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as caller
  participant B as callee
  A->>B: call ¹
  B-->>A: result
  Note over A,B: what holds across the flow ²
```

`state`:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  s(["start"]) --> a["state"]
  a ==>|"[owner] move"| b["state"]
  b -.->|"fault ¹"| n["new state"]
  class n agent
  classDef agent stroke:#4c9be8,stroke-width:3px
```

`interface`, the public members only:

```mermaid
classDiagram
  direction LR
  class before["Module, before"] {
    member(arg) Result
  }
  class after["Module, after"] {
    member(arg) Result
    added(arg) Result ¹
  }
  before ..> after : adds one
```

`contract`, the shape after the change, the field it adds or changes marked:

```mermaid
classDiagram
  direction LR
  class Record {
    field string
    added string ¹
  }
  class Part {
    field number
  }
  Record --> Part : holds
  class Record:::agent
  classDef agent stroke:#4c9be8,stroke-width:3px
```
